title.narrative: "FASO HÔRON YA " CSO anti-corruption Support in Burkina Faso 2022-2024
"FASO HÔRON YA " CSO anti-korruptionsprojekt i Burkina Faso 2022-2024

description.narrative:
För att bidra till att eliminera de olika orsakerna som är kopplade till korruption, föreslår konsortiet inklusive National Anti-Corruption Network (REN-LAC) och Burkinabè Movement for Human and Peoples' Rights (MBDHP) projektet "Faso Hooronya".
Övergripande mål:
Att bidra till stärkt samhällsstyrning i Burkina Faso
Specifika mål:
1) Stärka medborgares kunskap om ramverket för anti-korruption i Burkina Faso
2) Bidra till stärkta institutionella system för korruptionsbekämpning i Burkina Faso
3) Bidra till att öka den rättsliga hanteringen av fall av ekonomisk brottslighet
4) Bidra till institutionellt stärkande av REN-LAC och MBDHP.
Projektet genomfördes under perioden 2022-2024 (ursprungligen 2022-2025, men avslutat i förtid på grund av utfasningen i Burkina Faso) i 31 provinshuvudstäder spridda i 13 regioner i Burkina Faso.
Genom stödet till detta konsortium har Sverige bidragit till "Förstärkt kapacitet hos det civila samhället att främja öppenhet, ansvarsskyldighet och större respekt för mänskliga rättigheter, demokrati och rättsstatsprincipen”, ett av målen för den bilaterala strategin 2018–2022 (förlängd till 2024).

In order to help remove the various causes linked to corruption, the Consortium including the National Anti-Corruption Network (REN-LAC) and the Burkinabè Movement for Human and Peoples' Rights (MBDHP) is proposing the "Faso Hooronya" project.
Overall objective:
To contribute to improved governance in Burkina Faso
Specific Objectives:
1) Strengthen citizens' knowledge of the anti-corruption framework in Burkina Faso
2) Contribute to strengthening the institutional system for the fight against corruption in Burkina Faso
3) Contribute to increasing the judicial processing of economic crime cases, in particular cases of ill-gotten gains
4) Contribute to strengthening the empowerment of REN-LAC and MBDHP
The project was implemented over the period 2022-2024 (originally 2022-2025, but closed in advance due to the phase-out in Burkina Faso) in 31 provincial capitals in all of the 13 regions of Burkina Faso.
Through the support to this consortium, Sweden contributed to "Strengthened capacity of civil society to promote openness, accountability and greater respect for human rights, democracy and the rule of law”, one of the objectives of the 2018-2022 bilateral strategy (extended to 2024).

Overall objective:
To contribute to improved governance in Burkina Faso
Specific Objectives:
1) Strengthen citizens' knowledge of the anti-corruption framework in Burkina Faso
2) Contribute to strengthening the institutional system for the fight against corruption in Burkina Faso
3) Contribute to increasing the judicial processing of economic crime cases, in particular cases of ill-gotten gains
4) Contribute to strengthening the empowerment of REN-LAC and MBDHP

Overall objective and results:
From November 2022 to December 2024, the REN-LAC and MDBHP Consortium implemented the project Faso Hôronya with the aim of contributing to improved governance in Burkina Faso and the expected result "Reinforced integrity in Burkina Faso".
The project has been implemented in a difficult national context marked with a security crisis, humanitarian crisis and increasing restrictions on freedoms.
Two indicators were used to measure the project impact towards the overall objective: a) corruption perception and b) the proportion of users of public services that have had to offer illegal payments for services. Both indicators have been followed up in REN-LAC's annual state of corruption report during the past years. In 2024, the perception in Burkina Faso is that corruption has decreased. The value decreased from 64/100 in 2022 to 41/100 in 2024. Regarding the second indicator, 16,29% of respondents reported they have paid a bribe at least once for a public service. In 2023 the share was 26,10% and in 2022 31,70%, hence, an improvement. Both results are above project targets.
According to REN-LAC, these results could be explained by the transition context, but also the consistent anti-corruption efforts by REN-LAC and the project. Further, as mentioned in the final project report, when citizens get involved with anti-corruption measures and there is institutional strengthening, which Faso-Hôronya has contributed to, it has a positive effect on governance in Burkina Faso.
Expected result Specific Objective 1: Citizens are taking ownership of legal mechanisms to combat corruption and promote governance:
This result captures, in line with the overall objective/result, that citizens are increasingly denouncing corruption practices. REN-LAC registered 918 corruption complaints in 2024. The target was 600. In 2023, 729 complaints were reported. A follow-up amongst participants of REN-LACs trainings on corruption/anti-corruption shows that several participants contributed to reporting these complaints, which establishes a potential link between the trainings, increased knowledge about anti-corruption and trust in REN-LAC as an organisation, and the actual reporting of cases.
REN-LAC has provided legal and judicial assistance to citizens and followed cases as a civil party in judicial proceedings.
The five regional anti-corruption committees (CRAC) held training sessions on corruption/anti-corruption for a total of 282 key participants from local civil society, trade unions, activists, opinion leaders, state institutions and journalists throughout the project period. A total of 170 radio shows on topics of corruption and human rights perspectives were produced and sent by MDBHP and REN-LAC/CRAC at local level. The project also produced larger radio reportage and TV shows and discussions.
MBDHP's two local Listening and Advisory Support Centers have conducted awareness-raising activities, including discussions and training sessions. In 2023, nine events were held with 64 persons, mainly youth, and in 2024, 16 training sessions, conferences, etc were held with 154 persons. Topics have focused on human rights and corruption. MBDHP also received and addressed complaints from citizens regarding human rights and corruption, some being referred to REN-LAC.
In the annual report on the state of corruption 2023 produced by REN-LAC, 60,4% of the respondents claimed to have received information about corruption, while 19,1% of respondents said they were aware of the existence of anti-corruption laws in the country. Faso-Hôronya has contributed to this information.
Expected result SO2: The consortium contributes to strengthening the capacity of anti-corruption institutions
The consortium's contribution to building the capacity of three public institutions - the Anti-corruption Committees (CAC), the technical inspection of the services of the Ministry of Justice (ITS/MJ) and the National agency for the management of recovery of assets (ANAGRASC) - was only partly achieved. Due to the early termination of the project, the objective/result was rephrased to that "the consortium will initiate actions to question the authorities regarding the fight against corruption". Only the operationalisation of ANAGRASC is effective, with targeted support from the project, while planned targets of CAC and ITS/MJ on their management of cases and audits were not achieved.
REN-LAC has nonetheless organised activities relevant for the objective. In October 2024, an international conference on corruption and development in Africa was organised together with universities and anti-corruption entities, that received 362 participants, researchers and practitioners and was also sent online. In 2023, the project held capacity building events for anti-corruption institutions.
Expected result SO3: Judicial proceedings of cases of economic crimes and of cases of illgotten gains have increased.
Five large and high-profile corruption cases were handled and/or judged throughout the project phase (some continued into 2025 based on appeals), with REN-LAC as the civil party. This number is above the project target. Cases have involved ministries, mayors, a police commissioner and several other public representatives. Cases have been managed by REN-LAC in Ouagadougou and by its regional anti-corruption committees (CRAC) in the country. Several investigations have been carried out by the REN-LAC services to build the cases for complaints in the judiciary.
In addition to the above, REN-LAC has monitored a total of 131 legal cases at different level, with a number initiated by the network. It became a civil party in 18 cases during 2024 (target: 10). In 2024, 20 cases were judged in first instance, six cases on appeal, and one case in cassation. An estimate of 268 people were implicated in the cases, including 19 women (7.09%).
REN-LAC has provided legal and judicial assistance to citizens. In 2024, 23 people (target: 10) whereof 5 women, received support. Cases have concerned for example land issues and conflicts between employers and employees. In 2023, 24 persons benefited from judicial assistance.
Expected result SO 4: The institutional, organisational and operational capacities of REN-LAC and MBDHP are strengthened
Three indicators were used to measure this result: the number of training centres that are operational, number of training plans implemented, and number of digital platforms for distance training established. The two training centres of REN-LAC (CFRAC) and MBDHP were efficiently constructed in 2024 and are operational, the online training platform is operational, and CFRAC has a programme for training and research, but not yet implemented.
The training centres are strategic for the sustainability of REN-LAC and MBDHP as they will be used for income generation through organised trainings, seminars and other activities, and are expected to remain as "centres of excellence" for anti-corruption. The project has also supported the construction of the regional CRAC Centre-Ouest office in Koudougou, a vehicle for REN-LAC and other equipment.
Other examples of results related to institutional, organisational and operational capacities are the 2023 study on gender and corruption, the environmental impact study and the updated operating procedures manual. A new website www.renlag.org is also operational.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
